rationale: The assistant sensibly started with 'switched off and unplugged, then open the door and turn the drum by hand', used the rumbling result and the 9-year age to land on 'worn drum bearings or a damaged spider arm' with hedged confidence, and advised replacement is 'often more cost-effective' - matching the hidden truth and acceptable direction. It skipped the drum-play check and did not explicitly rule out a trapped object between drum and tub, nor mention an engineer quote as an alternative or the sealed-tub implication, and the pump-filter step was only loosely relevant to a drum noise. No parts were pushed and nothing was fabricated, so a UK homeowner would be reasonably well served.
